name: BQ78350DBTR-R1A
title: CEDV gas gauge and battery management controller for the BQ769x0 AFE family
summary: BQ78350-R1A is a battery management controller that works beside a BQ769x0 analog front end in Li-ion and LiFePO4 packs of 3 to 15 series cells (BQ76920: 3 to 5, BQ76930: 6 to 10, BQ76940: 9 to 15). It reads cell voltages, current and temperature from the AFE over I2C, runs a compensated end-of-discharge-voltage (CEDV) fuel gauge and state-of-health estimate, balances cells, applies voltage, current and temperature protection and logs lifetime data. A host reads it over SMBus 1.1; it can drive a 5-segment LED or LCD state-of-charge display and supports SHA-1 authentication. It runs from 2.5 V supplied by the AFE, in a 30-pin TSSOP.
key_figures: up to 320 A charge and discharge
VCC 2.4 V to 2.6 V (2.5 V nom)
650 μA typ; SLEEP 300 μA typ; SHUTDOWN 0.1 μA typ
SMBus 1.1, slave, optional PEC; up to 8 resistor-set addresses

circuits.title: 5-series cell typical schematic, gas gauge section
circuits.description: The gauge half of a 5-cell pack with a BQ76920 AFE. U2 runs from the AFE's 2.5 V REGOUT with C24 at VCC, R55 holding MRST high and C25 on RBI. The pack voltage reaches BAT through a divider (R47 over R48 with C23) that only conducts while VEN is high: VEN, pulled up by R51, turns on Q9, which pulls Q8's gate low through R50 so Q8 connects BATT+ to the divider; R49 holds Q8 off otherwise. ALERT, SDA and SCL go straight to the AFE. The SMBus reaches the J4 connector through series resistors (R72 and R77 on SMBC, R70 and R80 on SMBD), with 5.6 V Zeners, 1 MΩ pulldowns and spark gaps E2 and E4. DISP is pulled to REGOUT by R57. PRECHG leaves as PRE to the precharge driver in the AFE section.
notes: Pins 21 (GPIO A) and 28 (GPIO B) are tied to VSS; pin 1 (COM), the LED outputs, ADREN, SAFE and PWRM are left open.
The SMBus lines at J4 are for setting up the gauge; use in a system needs an isolation circuit on them.

circuits.title: 5-series cell typical schematic, AFE section
circuits.description: The BQ76920 half of the same pack. Five cells on J1 reach VC0 to VC5 through 100 Ω resistors with 1 µF filter capacitors; the AFE's BAT and REGSRC are fed from BATT+ through D11 and R12 with C15. R60 (1 mΩ) senses current between BATT- and the low-side FETs, filtered to SRP and SRN by R59, R61 and C27 to C29. Back-to-back N-channel FETs Q12 (discharge, driven from DSG through R63) and Q15 (charge, driven from CHG through Q16, R69 and D27) sit between the sense resistor and PACK-. Q13 with R64 makes a 1 kΩ precharge path around Q15, switched on through Q14 when the gauge pulls PRE low. RT1 on TS1 senses temperature; S1 with R36 wakes the AFE for boot. The AFE's REGOUT, with C21, supplies the gauge and the 10 kΩ SDA and SCL pullups.
notes: GND joins BATT- only through the net tie NT1.
Q13 pins: 1 gate, 2 source, 3 drain. Q12 and Q15 pins: 1, 2, 3 source, 4 gate, 5 to 8 drain.
The firmware defaults are set for a five-series, 4400 mAh pack on a BQ76920.

operation.text: The controller pairs with a BQ769x0 AFE for 3 to 15 series cells and capacities up to 320 Ah. It gauges charge, estimates state of health, balances cells and protects on voltage, current and temperature. Host access is SMBus 1.1; state of charge can be shown on LEDs or an LCD; history and diagnostic records sit in non-volatile memory and are read over the same bus.
Configurable cell overvoltage and undervoltage, charge and discharge overcurrent, short circuit, and charge and discharge overtemperature with separate alarms and thresholds per thermistor.

More serious faults can drive the SAFE pin, which can blow an in-line fuse and disable the pack for good. These faults are safety overvoltage and undervoltage, safety overcurrent and overtemperature in charge and discharge, faults in the charge, precharge or discharge FET, cell imbalance, an open thermistor and loss of AFE communication.

The charge algorithm and its responses are configurable. The device reports the current wanted for constant-current charging and the voltage wanted for constant-voltage charging, supports precharge and 0 V charging, and inhibits or suspends charge when pack temperature leaves its window.
CEDV gauging integrates charge and discharge current, corrects the charge measurement for temperature and state of charge, and estimates self-discharge with a temperature correction.

Logged for warranty and analysis: maximum and minimum temperature, maximum and minimum voltage of each cell, cycle count, peak charge and discharge current, and the 12 most common safety events that update SafetyStatus().
A host can authenticate the pack with SHA-1.

The AFE's 15-bit integrating coulomb counter measures VSR = V(SRP) - V(SRN) across a small sense resistor over -0.20 V to 0.20 V with 15 µV resolution; positive VSR is charge, negative is discharge. The controller reads the AFE registers and integrates the result over time. Reported current can be scaled for large packs through SpecificationInfo().

Each cell voltage is read through the AFE's 14-bit ADC (input range up to 6.075 V) once a second, scaled to mV and used for balancing and per-cell faults. Separately, the average cell voltage used by the gauge comes from an external translation divider at BAT, switched on by VEN only when needed; VEN needs a pullup to VCC, typically 100 kΩ. VAUX is an optional auxiliary input sampled once a second and reported scaled over SMBus. Voltage reports can be scaled for large packs through SpecificationInfo().

Temperature comes from the AFE's internal sensor or its external thermistors; the AFE offers one, two or three thermistor inputs depending on its cell count. By default an external NTC on the BQ76920 feeds Temperature(), converted by a polynomial to 0.1 °C resolution; the default coefficients suit a Semitec 103AT.

NORMAL: measurement, calculation, protection and data updates every 1 s, with reduced power between. SLEEP: the same at an adjustable interval. SHUTDOWN: fully powered down. PWRM shows which mode the device is in.

SMBus 1.1, slave only, with optional packet error checking. The slave address can be set by a voltage on SMBA from a pair of high-value resistors, read when leaving POR or when system presence is detected; ADREN can switch that divider off afterwards. By default the feature is off and the address is 0x16; resistor selection allows up to nine addresses. With SMBC and SMBD both low for 2 s or more the device enters the bus-off state; either line going high clears it and the bus is ready within 1 ms.

Parameters are set with the Battery Management Studio (BQSTUDIO) tool and saved as a golden image. As shipped the device suits a 5-series, 4400 mAh pack on a BQ76920 and keeps CHG, DSG and PCHG FETs off, with many features disabled, until the ManufacturingStatus() bit enabling ManufacturerAccess() commands is received or the default Manufacturing Status is changed. Setup falls into measurement, gas gauging, charging, protection and peripheral features.

The AFE Cell Map register names which AFE inputs carry cells. Cell voltages are reported in stack order: three cells wired to VC1, VC2 and VC5 still appear as CellVoltage1() to CellVoltage3(). Offset calibration of each is available.

On by default (DA Configuration [ExtAveEN] = 1); the VEN-switched divider at BAT gives ExtAveCellVoltage(). With CEDV Gauging Config [ExtAveCell] = 1 (the default) tolerance and temperature drift of the divider resistors and FETs add measurement and gauging error. Offset and gain calibration are available.

The default Chem ID is 1210, a LiCoO2 chemistry, and default maximum capacity is 4400 mAh; both are changed to match the cells. CEDV gauging uses seven coefficients whose defaults are generic for LiCoO2 and are recalculated for accuracy.

Out of the box the charge algorithm targets a nominal 18 V, 4400 mAh pack with CC/CV. Charge voltage is set per cell and ChargingVoltage() reports the pack total. Fast charging current defaults to 2000 mA. Depending on temperature, voltage and faults, the device reports reduced or zero ChargingVoltage() and ChargingCurrent().
Default protection settings are conservative and meant for bench evaluation; they must not be raised beyond the safe limits of the cell manufacturer or of any industry standard.
By default up to five LEDs form a bar graph of RemainingStateOfCharge(), 20% per LED, lit when DISP goes low and held for a programmable time. LED count and thresholds are configurable.
At power-up VCC, MRST, VEN and PWRM rise together. After a short boot the device starts updating data; VEN pulsing for the ExtAveCell() measurement marks normal operation.

VCC comes straight from the 2.5 V REGOUT of the BQ769x0. A 0.1 µF capacitor from VCC to VSS is required, placed tight against the device, and a 100 kΩ resistor from MRST to VCC is required for a correct power-up.

Put the VCC capacitor beside the IC with the shortest traces, keeping its loop small; ideally both traces are equal in length and run the same way, and a via near the VSS pin goes to a ground plane. The RBI capacitor placement is not critical and may sit farther away.

Keep MRST connections as short as possible. MRST may tie directly to VCC when reset is not needed. Against unwanted resets: 0.1 µF from MRST to ground, a 1 kΩ pullup to VCC, or a ground pattern around the circuit. A test point on MRST needs a 10 kΩ series resistor.

The 5.6 V Zeners guarding the communication pins go as close to the pack connector as possible, and their ground ends return to PACK(-), not to the digital ground. A spark gap at the connector with 0.2 mm spacing between points protects SMBus clock, data and other lines.
